segments.text:
V. 7.
Go w•ſh at the pool of Siloam—Perhaps our LORD intended to make the Miracle more taken Notice of. For a Crowd of People would naturally gather round him, to obſerve the Event of ſo ſtrange a Preſcription. And it is exceeding probable, the Guide who muſt have led him in traverſing a great Part of the City, would mention the Errand he was going upon, and ſo call thoſe who ſaw him to a greater Attention.

From the Fountain of Siloam, which was without the Walls of Jeruſalem, a little Stream flowed into the City, and was received in a Kind of Baſon, near the Temple, and called the Pool of Siloam. Which is, by interpretation, Sent—And ſo was a Type of the Meſſiah, who was ſent of GOD. He want and wiſhed, and came ſeeing—He believed, and obeyed, and found a Bleſſing. Had he been wiſe in his own Eyes, and reaſoned like Naaman, on the Impropriety of the Means, he had juſtly been leſt in Darkneſs. LORD, may our proud Hearts be ſubdued to the Methods of thy recovering Grace! May we have Thee to chuſe, how Thou wilt beſtow Favours, which it is our higheſt Intereſt to receive on any Tearms.
